role.altitude: From running HR services and answering escalations to designing Noordhaven's HR operating system: which agents run which steps (policy desk, budget model, CAO watch, forecast), where people approve, what is logged, and what the works council has agreed to.
reach: People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: first-pass driver analysis of verzuim and 90-day attrition, using the analyst's metric layer
FP&A Analyst: personnel cost budget and the monthly variance against AFAS actuals
HR Business Partner: routine policy questions from managers, handled through a gated policy desk
Compensation and Benefits Specialist: costing CAO wage demands and job grading options
Controller: flex worker spend reconciliation across the three staffing agency portals
role.ceiling_note: About 35-40% of the role's 1,600 hours can shift: policy questions, analysis, budgets, CAO and legislation study, and forecasting. Leading the 13-person team, hearings, CAO bargaining, works council consultation, harassment and conflict cases, and accountability for high-risk AI (recruitment, evaluation, termination, from 2 Dec 2027) stay with the director.
skills_to_grow: Setting autonomy levels, gates and audit logs per agent, and reading those logs
EU AI Act classification and AI literacy duties (Art. 4, Art. 50, Annex III) for HR systems
Writing an AI policy and agreeing it with the works council (WOR Art. 24 and Art. 27)
Scenario-based workforce and cost planning on AFAS data
Costing union demands on AI 'zeggenschap' for the 2027 CAO round
role.ambitious_version: An HR operating system where every manager on three sites gets a cited policy answer within minutes, every month starts with a scenario-based forecast of hires, flex demand and verzuim per site, and every CAO or law change is costed before it lands. The director spends the freed time on the North Star: 90-day retention of warehouse hires and manager satisfaction, and on an AI agreement with the works council and unions that Noordhaven can point to.

tasks.short: Lead the HR team of 13: set priorities, check progress, unblock people, review their work.

today.trigger: Daily: weekly team meeting, one-to-ones, escalations from HRBPs, recruiters and payroll.
steps: Scan Outlook and Teams for escalations and status
Hold one-to-ones and the weekly team meeting
Check progress on open vacancies, verzuim cases and month close
Review and sign off drafts from HRBPs and admins
Reassign work when someone is absent or a peak hits
drudgery: Collecting status from several people and systems before each meeting
today.time_sinks: Assembling a picture of who is doing what across AFAS, Recruitee and mail before the director can decide anything.

lenses.faster: A Monday briefing is compiled from Recruitee, AFAS verzuim and payroll status, so the team meeting starts from facts instead of a round of updates.
lenses.autonomous: Overdue actions and stalled vacancies are flagged automatically to the owner, with the director copied only after a second miss.
lenses.ambitious: Proper one-to-ones with every team member every two weeks, with a written development plan, which today slips in busy months.
lenses.joy: Less status chasing; more time for coaching and the hard cases that need judgement.
lenses.options: For a capacity crunch (season peak, two people out), get three staffing options with their effect on time to hire and month close.
lenses.altitude: The director designs who and which agent owns each HR step, and sets the autonomy and gates per agent, as Workday customers now do.
reach: Taking over agent governance (the 'agent management' job Bersin describes) instead of creating a separate role

tasks.human_edge: Trust, coaching, judging people's performance and wellbeing, and being accountable for the team's decisions.
tasks.pattern_why: Leading people is the job; AI only prepares briefings and tracks actions.

in_practice.trigger: Every Monday 07:00 and on any item overdue more than five working days.
steps: Pull open vacancies and stage age from Recruitee
Pull open verzuim cases and poortwachter deadlines from AFAS
Pull month-close status from the payroll checklist in SharePoint
Draft a one-page briefing with risks and owners
Director reviews and uses it in the team meeting
in_practice.human_gate: The director decides priorities and reassignments; the briefing only proposes.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint HR team site, weekly briefing archive

evidence.claim: Workday customers set which agent tasks run alone, which need review and who approves, with each action logged.
Agent management is seen by analysts as a new HR job.
Microsoft 365 Copilot can summarise Teams meetings and mail threads into action lists.

risks: Briefings that pull verzuim data could expose medical detail beyond need-to-know (AVG)
Team members may feel monitored if action tracking is used to judge them; works council may need to consent (WOR Art. 27)
research_questions: How many hours a week does the director spend collecting status today? (time log for two weeks)
Can AFAS and Recruitee data be joined reliably without manual cleaning?
Does the works council see automatic overdue flags as a personnel monitoring system that needs consent?

tasks.short: Answer managers' questions on policy (leave, conduct, harassment, equal treatment) and propose policy changes.

today.trigger: A manager mails or calls with a question, or an incident or complaint comes in.
steps: Read the question and find the relevant policy in SharePoint
Check the CAO article and any law (Arbowet, AWGB)
Write or phone an answer to the manager
For serious cases, open a file and involve the HRBP or confidential adviser
Note recurring questions and propose a policy change to MT and works council
drudgery: Looking up the same CAO articles again and again
Answering the same leave and overtime questions for three sites
today.time_sinks: Routine questions from 60+ team leads that each need a lookup across two CAOs and the policy library.

lenses.faster: A policy desk answers routine questions with citations to the CAO article and policy page; the director sees only escalations.
lenses.autonomous: Questions in a Teams channel get a cited draft answer in minutes; answers on settled topics go out after an HR Administrator checks them.
lenses.ambitious: Every team lead on night shift in Venlo gets a correct answer in the same hour, and HR gets a monthly report of which policies confuse people.
lenses.joy: No more retyping leave rules; the director keeps the conversations that matter: conduct, conflict, harassment.
lenses.options: For a policy change, draft three wordings with their cost and works council implications.
lenses.altitude: The director owns the knowledge base, the escalation rules and the monthly review of wrong or unclear answers.
reach: HR Business Partner routine manager questions
HR Administrator first-line questions on contracts and leave

tasks.human_edge: Harassment, discrimination and conflict cases need trust, confidentiality and judgement, and the legal duty sits with the employer.
tasks.pattern_why: Routine questions have clear sources and checkable answers; a person approves before the answer counts, and sensitive topics route straight to a human.

in_practice.trigger: A manager posts a question in the HR Teams channel or the policy mailbox.
steps: Classify the question: routine, sensitive (harassment, discrimination, conflict) or unknown
Sensitive goes straight to an HRBP or confidential adviser, no AI answer
Routine: retrieve CAO article and policy page, draft an answer with citations
HR Administrator or HRBP approves or edits; answer is sent with a chatbot disclosure
Weekly: cluster unclear topics into proposed policy changes for the director
in_practice.human_gate: HR staff approve each answer before it goes out; the director approves policy changes before MT and works council.
systems: Microsoft 365 Copilot or a retrieval agent on SharePoint
data_needed: Escalation list and confidential adviser contacts
Log of past questions and answers
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint list with question, sources cited, approver and final answer

evidence.claim: IBM's AskHR handled 16 million messages in 2025 with CSAT +74, after an early failure when human HR routes were removed too soon (NPS -35).
At IBM India 90-95% of HR questions go through an assistant while accountability stays with people.
Chatbots must disclose they are AI (EU AI Act Art. 50).

risks: A wrong answer on dismissal, overtime pay or leave creates a claim or union dispute
Removing the human route too early, as IBM learned
research_questions: What share of the last three months of manager questions were routine and answerable from CAO plus policy text?
How accurate are cited answers on a test set of 50 real questions, checked by an HRBP?
Does the works council want a say in the policy desk under its Art. 24 AI discussion?

tasks.short: Dig into verzuim, turnover and hiring numbers to find causes and propose policy fixes.

today.trigger: Monthly HR dashboard review, or a site manager raises a problem (high verzuim, early leavers).
steps: Open Power BI dashboards on the nightly AFAS extract
Export to Excel and slice by site, shift, team and contract type
Ask the People Analytics Analyst for extra cuts
Read exit interview notes and HRBP observations
Write recommendations for the MT
drudgery: Rebuilding the same Excel pivots each month
Waiting for ad-hoc cuts from the one analyst
today.time_sinks: Back-and-forth with the analyst to test each hypothesis, and reading free-text exit notes by hand.

lenses.faster: Ask questions of the analyst's metric layer in plain language and get the cut plus a chart, instead of waiting days.
lenses.autonomous: Each month a drift report flags sites or teams where verzuim or 90-day leavers moved beyond a set range.
lenses.ambitious: Link 90-day retention to recruitment source, agency, onboarding completion in Studytube and first team lead, for every hire, not once a year.
lenses.joy: No more pivot rebuilding; the director spends time on why the numbers move and talks to the sites.
lenses.options: Three explanations for a verzuim spike, each with the data that supports or weakens it and a test to run.
lenses.altitude: The director defines the questions and metric definitions with the analyst and checks the reasoning, not the spreadsheet.
reach: People Analytics and HRIS Analyst first-pass analysis

tasks.human_edge: Knowing the sites, the team leads and the context behind the numbers, and choosing which fix to back.
tasks.pattern_why: The data is structured but causes need judgement; AI speeds analysis on a governed metric layer, the director draws conclusions.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly AFAS refresh; monthly drift report on the first working day.
steps: Run fixed metric checks on verzuim, turnover and 90-day retention per site and shift
Flag movements outside agreed ranges
Director asks follow-up questions through Copilot in Power BI
LLM clusters themes from exit interview notes
Director drafts recommendations with the analyst
in_practice.human_gate: Recommendations go to MT only after the director and the analyst agree on the evidence.
in_practice.logs_to: Power BI workspace and a SharePoint analysis log

evidence.claim: Copilot in Power BI answers natural-language questions over a semantic model and drafts report pages.
evidence.source: model knowledge (Microsoft Copilot in Power BI)

evidence.claim: Digest recommends copilot on the people analyst's metric layer, autonomy 2, scenarios rather than one number.

risks: Small teams make individuals identifiable in verzuim cuts (AVG)
Correlation read as cause, leading to wrong policy
Monitoring of individuals would need works council consent and could become high-risk AI from Dec 2027
research_questions: Are metric definitions in the AFAS extract stable enough for self-service questions?
What minimum group size keeps verzuim cuts anonymous?
Did the last three recommendations to MT rest on analysis the tool could have produced?

tasks.short: Plan and steer the HR year: recruitment, training, labour relations and works council agenda.

today.trigger: Annual HR plan, quarterly MT reviews, season peaks, CAO and works council calendar.
steps: Draft the annual HR plan and quarterly priorities
Plan the works council meetings and items needing advice or consent
Align training plans for forklift, VCA and food safety with L&D
Plan flex capacity with sites and agencies for peaks
Report progress to MT
drudgery: Chasing certificate expiry lists from Studytube
today.time_sinks: Pulling status from many owners and systems to update the plan and the MT deck.

lenses.faster: A draft quarterly plan and MT deck are built from the action list, Studytube expiries and vacancy data.
lenses.autonomous: Certificate expiries and works council deadlines raise tasks to the owner without the director reminding them.
lenses.ambitious: A proper labour relations calendar covering both CAOs, the works council and the 2027 union demands on AI, kept current.
lenses.joy: Less deck building, more time with site managers and the works council.
lenses.options: Three plan variants for next year: lean, base and growth, each with headcount, training and flex cost.
lenses.altitude: The director designs the planning cycle and the AI policy for HR, and agrees it with the works council in the Art. 24 meeting.

tasks.human_edge: Choosing priorities, negotiating with MT, unions and the works council, and being accountable for the plan.
tasks.pattern_why: Planning is judgement and negotiation; AI drafts and keeps the calendar.

in_practice.trigger: Quarter start and each works council meeting cycle.
steps: Collect status from action list, Recruitee, Studytube and agency portals
Draft plan update and MT slides
Generate plan variants with cost estimates
Director edits and decides
Publish to SharePoint and assign owners
in_practice.human_gate: Director approves the plan; works council items go through the formal procedure.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint HR plan library with version history

evidence.claim: Works council should discuss AI policy in the Art. 24 meeting; some decisions need advice or consent.
FNV asks for worker 'zeggenschap' over AI and AI literacy training at the CAO table.
Transport CAO runs to 31 Dec 2026, so the 2027 round is now.

risks: A polished draft plan can hide weak assumptions
Missing a works council consent step for an AI tool makes the decision voidable
research_questions: How many hours per quarter go into plan updates and MT decks today?
Can Studytube expiries be pulled automatically by site and certificate?
Which planned AI uses does the works council consider consent-requiring under Art. 27?

tasks.short: Build the yearly personnel budget and track spend against it each month.

today.trigger: Annual budget round with Finance; monthly variance review after payroll close.
steps: Export headcount and salaries from AFAS to Excel
Apply CAO raises, step increases and employer charges
Add flex worker, recruitment and training costs
Agree the budget with the Finance Director and FP&A
Each month compare actuals and explain variances
drudgery: Applying CAO tables by hand per employee
today.time_sinks: Rebuilding the Excel model each year and explaining variances line by line.

lenses.faster: A budget model computes cost per position from AFAS records and CAO tables; the director checks assumptions instead of formulas.
lenses.autonomous: After payroll close the variance report runs and flags lines outside tolerance with likely causes.
lenses.ambitious: A rolling forecast per site and month, including flex, instead of one annual budget that is stale by March.
lenses.joy: No more Excel formula hunting; time goes to the trade-offs with Finance.
lenses.options: Cost of each CAO outcome (e.g. 3%, 4%, 5% raise) and of more fixed versus flex staff.
lenses.altitude: The director owns the assumptions and rules in the model; FP&A and the model do the arithmetic.

tasks.human_edge: Negotiating trade-offs with Finance and MT and owning the assumptions.
tasks.pattern_why: Positions, CAO scales and charges are structured rules with checkable output; build once, run without a model.

in_practice.trigger: Annual budget kick-off; monthly after payroll close.
steps: Pull positions, scales and FTE from AFAS
Apply CAO tables, step increases, charges and pension changes
Add flex cost from agency portal data
Produce budget and monthly variance with flags
Director and FP&A review and approve
in_practice.human_gate: Director and Finance Director sign off the budget; variances are explained by people.
data_needed: CAO wage tables and raise dates
in_practice.logs_to: Versioned model in SharePoint; Power BI variance report

evidence.claim: Digest suggests deterministic software from AFAS positions and CAO tables, autonomy 3.
Power Query and Power BI can model position-level costs from an AFAS extract.

risks: Wrong CAO table or pension change silently skews the budget
Agency data formats differ across three portals
research_questions: Can all three agency portals export hours and rates in a machine-readable format?
How large were last year's budget variances and what caused them?
Who maintains the CAO tables in the model after each new agreement?

tasks.short: Keep up with labour law, court rulings and CAO changes, and judge what they mean for us.

today.trigger: Newsletters, union and employer-association updates, new CAO texts, rulings in the press.
steps: Read newsletters from law firms, TLN, unions and AFAS
Read new CAO texts and rulings
Judge impact on Noordhaven
Brief MT, HRBPs and payroll
Update policies when needed
drudgery: Skimming many newsletters with little relevant content
today.time_sinks: Reading volume, most of it not relevant to logistics or the three sites.

lenses.faster: A weekly digest summarises only relevant changes, with citations and a first impact note.
lenses.autonomous: Sources are watched continuously; a new CAO text triggers a clause-by-clause comparison with the old one.
lenses.ambitious: Every change is costed and routed to the owner (payroll, HRBP, L&D) with a deadline, including AI Act duties.
lenses.joy: No more newsletter skimming; the director debates the meaning, not the reading.
lenses.options: For each major change, three response options with cost and risk.
lenses.altitude: The director curates the sources and checks the impact notes; the watch runs on its own.
reach: Payroll Specialist CAO wage table updates

tasks.human_edge: Judging impact on Noordhaven and deciding what to do, especially in bargaining.
tasks.pattern_why: Unstructured texts turned into cited summaries and diffs inside a fixed weekly workflow.

in_practice.trigger: Weekly schedule; any new CAO or major ruling.
steps: Collect items from chosen sources
LLM filters for relevance and summarises with citations
Compare CAO versions clause by clause
Director checks and marks actions
Route actions to owners
in_practice.human_gate: Director confirms impact before anything changes in policy or payroll.
data_needed: Source list (rechtspraak.nl, TLN, FNV, CNV, government sites)
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint legal watch list with sources and decisions

evidence.claim: Digest suggests llm_step summaries with citations, autonomy 3.
AI Act high-risk rules for recruitment and evaluation apply from 2 Dec 2027.

risks: A missed or misread change leads to wrong pay or policy
Summaries cite the wrong article version
research_questions: Does an LLM summary catch the changes an employment lawyer would flag in the last CAO revision?
Which sources can be pulled automatically and legally?
How many hours a month go to reading today?

tasks.short: Oversee job descriptions and grading in the CAO job classification, and settle grading disputes.

today.trigger: New or changed role, reorganisation, or an employee objects to a grade.
steps: Collect the job description from the manager
Compare with CAO reference jobs
Score the job with the grading method
Discuss with manager and, when disputed, the appeal committee
Record the grade in AFAS
today.time_sinks: Getting a usable job description from managers and preparing disputes.

lenses.faster: An assistant turns a manager's notes into a structured job description and lists the closest CAO reference jobs.
lenses.autonomous: Changed tasks in a role trigger a review flag instead of waiting for a complaint.
lenses.ambitious: All roles across three sites reviewed for consistency in one cycle, not once in years.
lenses.joy: Less rewriting; more time for the grading discussion.
lenses.options: Two or three grading proposals with the reasoning per factor.
lenses.altitude: The director sets the method and checks consistency; the assistant prepares files. Rate jobs, not people.
reach: Compensation and Benefits Specialist job description drafting

tasks.human_edge: Final grading, fairness across sites, and handling appeals with the works council and unions.
tasks.pattern_why: Grading affects pay and must be defensible; AI prepares, people decide.

in_practice.trigger: A new or changed role request in SharePoint.
steps: Manager fills a short form
LLM drafts the job description and matches reference jobs
Compensation Specialist scores the job
Director approves
Grade recorded in AFAS
data_needed: CAO job classification and reference jobs

evidence.claim: Digest suggests copilot, autonomy 2; rate jobs, not people.

risks: Bias toward wording rather than content of the job
Equal pay issues if grading is inconsistent
Tools that score people could fall under high-risk AI
research_questions: How many grading files and appeals were there last year?
Do LLM reference-job matches agree with expert scoring on past cases?
Will the works council accept AI-prepared files?

tasks.short: Forecast how many staff and flex workers we need per site and season.

today.trigger: Annual budget, sales forecasts, new customer contracts.
steps: Get volume forecasts from operations
Convert volumes to FTE with productivity norms
Subtract expected turnover and verzuim
Split fixed and flex need
Agree with site managers and Finance
today.time_sinks: Collecting inputs and rebuilding the model.

lenses.faster: A model converts volume forecasts into FTE need per site, shift and season.
lenses.autonomous: Monthly refresh with actual turnover, verzuim and volumes.
lenses.ambitious: Rolling 12-month forecast linked to recruitment and agency orders.
lenses.joy: Less spreadsheet work; more discussion with sites.
lenses.options: Scenarios: lost customer, new contract, high verzuim.
lenses.altitude: The director owns assumptions and scenarios.

tasks.human_edge: Judging business plans and choosing a scenario.
tasks.pattern_why: Data is structured but the plan needs judgement; scenarios rather than one number.

steps: Pull volumes, headcount, turnover and verzuim
Compute FTE need per scenario
Director reviews
Share with sites and Finance
in_practice.human_gate: Director and MT choose the scenario.

evidence.claim: Workday Work Intelligence (beta) cut planned hires from 50 to 42 in a demo.

risks: Bad volume forecasts make the output wrong
research_questions: How accurate were past forecasts?
Are productivity norms per site available?
Do sites trust a model forecast?
